newsitem.title: New Zealand: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Jan 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Jan 16.

text.p: Power companies are making a killing at their customer's expense, according to the Consumer Affairs Ministry. In a report made public on Wednesday, the ministry says that since deregulation in 1993 the companies have exploited their position as monopoly suppliers in a variety of ways. It says more than ten percent of domestic electricity meters have been in place unchanged, and in many cases not maintained, since 1956. Page 1.

The Conservation Department is understood to have shelved plans to cull 1000 Kaimanawa wild horses on-site this autumn, but will still muster them for selling or sending to abattoirs for pet food. A spokeswoman for Conservation Minister Nick Smith confirmed on Wednesday that the department would begin a massive muster of the horses this April or May, in a bid to save the rare species of the native tussock threatened by the herd. Page 1.

NZ First has spent $112,500 of taxpayers' money on coalition negotiations and is the only party to have accessed the $563,000 coalition fund set up by the government last year. Parliamentary Service Commission general manager John O'Sullivan said NZ First was the only party to have accessed the fund after $100,000 each, exclusive of GST, was allotted in an interim allocation for the use by National, Labour and NZ First during coalition talks. Page 2.

Youth Affairs Minister Deborah Morris wants the drinking age lowered to 18 and a national identity card introduced so the liquor law can be policed. Morris, an NZ First MP, said she supported the submission by the Youth Affairs Ministry on the review of liquor laws. The ministry is due to report to Justice Minister Doug Graham at the end of March. Page 3.

The New Zealand sharemarket's key NZSE 40 capital index is set to challenge its life-time peak this week after it surged to another three-year high on Wednesday on the back of a bond rally and continued strength of the Dow Jones. The NZSE 40 closed on
2431.30, up 25.10 points and just 8.3 points shy of its highest close, on February 3, 1994. Page 12.

Declining interest rates were offset by an "all time high" in median house prices to make martgages on average marginally less affordable in the December quarter, according to a Massey University survey. The university property studies' mortgage affordability survey recorded the tenth consecutive quarterly affordability decline, and showed that mortgage affordability dropped 7.4 percent in the year to December and fell 48 percent from the level of September 1994. Page 12.

Foster's unit Carlton and United Brewing won the takeover battle for Ballarat Brewing on Wednesday when Guinness Peat Group and Ballarat's directors accepted its offer of A$2.56 a Ballarat share. GPG director Maurice Loomes said on Wednesday night that GPG was certainly not disappointed with its near A$2.5 million (NZ$2.7) profit on the failed bid. It was happy to take the profit and was now looking around for the next investment opportunity. Page 12.

Treasurer and NZ First leader Winston Peters confirmed on Wednesday he would be responsible for the Reserve Bank once portfolio areas were delegated between himself and Associate Treasurer John Delamere. Peters was asked if the sharing of responsibilities had been decided between himself and Delamere, a NZ First colleague and the Te Tai Rawhiti MP. "It is being worked on and I have yet to have sufficient time with Mr Delamere ... We've had too much work on to decide that." he said. Page 12.

Registrar of companies Neville Harris has welcomed a Privy Council decision upholding his powers under the Securities Act. "This decision was critical to our continuing ability to protect the investing public of New Zealand," Harris said. The decision arose from an appeal by Culverden Retirement Village against the registrar's power to inspect documents under the Securities Act. Page 12.
